raw_response:
I am 63 this year, and with only 10.1 mu and two people in the house, I cannot farm like a big operator even if I understand the technical side. I still rely first on what has worked on my own land in Quzhou. Wheat-maize remains my backbone because it spreads risk and keeps grain coming in, but I keep some cotton because it fits my experience and gives me a cash crop if the price is decent. Since labor is tight and I am getting older, I will not put too much land into cotton. I would keep about 6.0 mu in the wheat-maize rotation and 4.1 mu in cotton. On wheat, I will stay with a stable local improved variety, sow in early October after basic tillage, and put most of the phosphorus and part of the nitrogen up front, then topdress at jointing. I will irrigate around sowing if the soil is dry, then at jointing and grain filling if needed, because wheat here usually pays back water better than cotton. After wheat harvest in June, I will move fast into summer maize on the same 6.0 mu with minimum tillage or direct seeding if I can hire the machine in time, because that turnaround window is short. For maize, I will use a hybrid, give a moderate fertilizer rate, and watch rainfall before deciding on one irrigation around tasseling. Cotton I will manage more cautiously: not too high an input level, enough base fertilizer to hold yield, one or two irrigations depending on rain, and spraying only when I actually see aphids, bollworm, or serious weeds. I do not chase the highest yield now. I want a steady crop, controlled cash cost, and some reserve in hand in case weather turns against me.
